subject.title: [Feature]: Add a visible browser panel to the Control UI for login handoff and browser management

question: What UX and security boundary should OpenClaw use for browser-login handoff before implementation starts?
rationale: The requested flow crosses authenticated browser-state exposure, operator authorization, redaction, write-control, and resume-policy choices that source inspection cannot settle mechanically.

options.title: Admin-scoped handoff panel
options.body: Add a browser-owned Control UI panel that starts read-only, requires explicit operator-gated write actions, and resumes the agent against the same tab/profile context.

options.title: Wait for plugin UI infrastructure
options.body: Defer browser handoff until the generic plugin UI entry-point or contribution-slot API lands, then implement the browser panel through that approved surface.

options.title: Keep primitives only
options.body: Leave browser status, tab, screenshot, and action control as CLI/RPC primitives and close the product request as out of scope for now.

recommendation.title: Admin-scoped handoff panel
recommendation.body: Add a browser-owned Control UI panel that starts read-only, requires explicit operator-gated write actions, and resumes the agent against the same tab/profile context.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest current routing signal for browser runtime/docs behavior and already commented on the canonical handoff direction.
